what_happened.line: The committee voted unanimously by roll call to try the DeWolfe royalty-free music license on a one-year contract.
Members compared DeWolfe, an annual license, with Storyblocks, which is discounted for the first year and then rises in price.
The October financial report's total column did not match the balance given; the manager will correct the spreadsheet and bring it to the next meeting.
The committee re-approved the September minutes and a short note will explain the missed October meeting, whose agenda was not posted in time.
Studio visits to Dracut and Westford are to be arranged, with no more than two members at each visit to avoid a quorum.

why_it_matters: The music license is a recurring cost paid from the cable program's budget, and DeWolfe's background-music rights last only while the subscription is active.
Studio equipment and architect spending compete for a limited budget, and the capital warrant article is the route to the cable money, so residents may be asked to vote on it at town meeting.
